document.title: How I Built Branqly – A Modern SaaS Link Shortener
document.excerpt: A breakdown of how I built and scaled Branqly with custom domain mapping, analytics, and auth flow.

body.raw:
> “Branqly is more than a link shortener — it’s a custom branding tool.”

## 🚀 The Idea Behind Branqly

While building projects, I often needed to share clean, trackable URLs. But most platforms lacked personalization or analytics. That's when the idea of **Branqly** hit me — a SaaS product that not only shortens URLs but gives full control to creators and developers.

## 🛠️ Tech Stack

- **Next.js (App Router)** – Full-stack React framework
- **MongoDB** – To store all URLs, users, and analytics data
- **ShadCN + Tailwind CSS** – UI components + design system
- **Vercel** – For deployment and edge performance
- **Resend** – For transactional emails (auth, reset, etc.)
- **Clerk** – For authentication
- **Chart.js** – For live analytics

## 🔐 Authentication Flow

I integrated Clerk for email/password and social auth. Once users logged in, they could manage all their custom links from a personalized dashboard.

## 🧠 Smart Features

- **Custom Domain Mapping**  
  Users can map their own domain (like `go.abhi.dev`) and manage links from there.

- **Real-Time Click Tracking**  
  Every short link tracks clicks in real-time and shows detailed analytics.

- **Link Expiry, Password Protection, & QR**  
  Users can protect links, set expiry timers, and generate QR codes.

## ⚙️ Challenges

- Setting up wildcard subdomain routing in Next.js was tricky.
- Optimizing MongoDB aggregation queries for analytics.
- Making the dashboard feel fast even with lots of links.

## 💡 What I Learned

This project pushed my full-stack skills, especially around auth, edge deployment, and DX. I also learned a lot about making things **production-ready** — like rate-limiting, server logs, and secure API access.

## 🧪 Demo & Source

- 🔗 [Live Site](https://branqly.xyz)
- 🧑‍💻 [GitHub Repo](https://github.com/abhi47025/branqly)

## ✨ Final Thoughts

Building Branqly taught me what it takes to ship a real SaaS product. It’s live, used by creators, and keeps improving with user feedback.

> Let me know what you think — and feel free to try it yourself at [Branqly.xyz](https://branqly.xyz)!
